1:72 to 75mm Miniature Scale for 3D Printing

Convert 3D printed tabletop miniatures from 1:72 to 75mm. This STL scale calculator is designed for Warhammer, D&D, and tabletop gaming miniatures.

Slicer Setting

308.6%

Uniform scale (XYZ locked)

Open in stlscale

The math

(75.0mm / 24.3mm) × 100 = 308.6%

Based on 175cm human baseline, eye-level measurement (160cm).

Scale baselines

  • Source eye level 22.2mm Eye
  • Target eye level 75.0mm Eye
  • Scale factor 308.6%

How I got this number

By kitsorix, 3D printing hobbyist

This percentage comes from a 175cm human baseline with eye-level at 160cm. I print the result and measure with calipers before I post it. If it looks wrong on my table, I adjust it.

I test every percentage on an FDM printer before publishing. PLA and PETG cool with minimal dimensional change — typically under 0.5%. If a number fails on my machine, I adjust it.

Full methodology →

When you need this

You need this when bringing older or smaller 1:72 models into a modern 75mm collection. This is a dramatic jump—more than double or less than half. The result is essentially a different model category. Use this only for deliberate artistic or display purposes, not mixed armies.

Source: 1:72

1:72 is the ratio. Popular for large army builds on a budget. Figures are roughly 20-22mm to the eyes. Common systems: Airfix, Revell, Zvezda.

Note: 1:72 scale creep exists: modern sculpts are often closer to 1:64.

Target: 75mm

75mm is used by Display busts, Figure painting competitions, Scale 75 display line. Not a tabletop wargaming scale. Designed for contest judging and display cabinets.

Note: 75mm sculpts often have separate heads or arms for easier painting access.

Print notes

Set your slicer to 308.6%. 75mm on FDM needs a 0.2mm nozzle and very slow print speeds for acceptable surface quality.

Data Correction

This number off?

I update these when enough people tell me something is wrong. If this ratio works differently on your machine, let me know.
